headline: Zcash jumps 7% on governance win as Democratic election sweep rattles then rebounds crypto markets
summary: A Democratic midterm sweep sent Bitcoin and stocks briefly lower overnight before both recovered — the market's read is that the political shift complicates the near-term regulatory picture for crypto, but not enough to sustain a selloff. Zcash was the day's standout, surging over 7% after its grants committee dropped a contested plan to redirect nearly 100,000 ZEC toward mining rewards, resolving a governance dispute that had weighed on the token for weeks. The Fear & Greed index sits at 34 — firmly in fear territory — suggesting the broader market remains cautious even as prices stabilized.

winners.name: Zcash
winners.catalyst: The Zcash grants committee reversed a proposal to redirect 98,000 ZEC toward future mining rewards, removing a supply-side overhang that had concerned holders. The governance resolution triggered a relief rally, pushing ZEC up over 7% to $1,278.95.

losers.name: Rain
losers.catalyst: No clear catalyst identified — the decline appears to reflect broader risk-off pressure on smaller-cap assets on a day of political uncertainty.

whyItMoved:
The overnight session was the most eventful part of the day. A Democratic sweep in U.S. midterm elections initially pushed Bitcoin and equities lower — markets read a Blue Wave as a headwind for crypto-friendly legislation, given that the current Democratic leadership has been more cautious on digital asset regulation than its Republican counterpart. But the selloff didn't hold. By the time U.S. markets opened, Bitcoin had recovered to $78,244, up 1.34% on the day, and Ethereum followed at +1.47% to $2,315. The rebound suggests traders concluded the political shift, while meaningful, doesn't change the near-term fundamentals enough to justify sustained selling.

Zcash was the day's clearest story. The grants committee's decision to drop its plan to redirect 98,000 ZEC — worth roughly $125 million at current prices — toward future mining rewards removed a specific, quantified concern about token supply. Governance disputes of this kind tend to suppress price until resolved; the resolution did the opposite, sending ZEC up 7.14%.

Elsewhere, Monero gained 2.67%, likely benefiting from the same privacy-coin attention that surrounded Zcash's news. Hyperliquid fell 3.34% with no clear catalyst — the move looks like broader risk-off pressure on smaller-cap assets during the overnight political volatility. The Fear & Greed index at 34 confirms the market's cautious posture: prices recovered, but sentiment did not.
